oneliner.t: Navy veteran and HR professional making her first run for office; unopposed in the July 21, 2026 Democratic primary (35,700 votes), she faces Rep. Paul Gosar on Nov. 3.

born.t: Austin, Texas (per Ballotpedia); date not documented

upbringing.t: Ballotpedia, drawing on her own survey, says she was born in Austin, Texas, has served in the U.S. Navy since 2015, earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Hawaii–West Oahu (2019) and a graduate degree from Grand Canyon University (2023), and works as an academic advisor and certified HR professional with a background in industrial-organizational psychology. A 2025 podcast describes her as a Navy veteran whose post-Navy work included social work and who is parenting while campaigning. Independent records for these details were not found.

career.role: U.S. Navy service (Ballotpedia: serving since 2015; podcast: veteran)

platform.t: Supports congressional term limits and removing big money from politics; signed the U.S. Term Limits pledge.
Fully funded schools, smaller classes, modernized classrooms.
Support small businesses and companies creating jobs in rural communities.
Lower prescription-drug costs, citing constituents who buy medication abroad.
Government standards for safe, ethical, transparent AI.
Paper ballots, transparent audits, protections for election workers, automatic voter registration, secure early and mail voting.
Use House investigative powers for fact-based accountability and careful use of taxpayer money.
